caption: 3 is not a quadratic residue mod 7
Listable in $n$: the residues mod 7 are 1, 2, 4
$-1$ is a residue mod $p$ exactly when $p\equiv1\pmod4$
Euler's criterion: $(a/p)\equiv a^{(p-1)/2}\pmod p$, here $3^3\equiv6\equiv-1$. See [[PowerMod]]
9 is not prime, so the call stays symbolic; see [[JacobiSymbol]]
wolfram.note: compute-engine's LegendreSymbol declines a non-prime modulus (per this example's name); Wolfram has no separate LegendreSymbol, so the emit uses JacobiSymbol (its closest counterpart), which is defined for any odd modulus and computes 1.
